verses.1:1: The words of the Convener, son of David, king in Jerusalem.
verses.1:2: "Vapor of vapors," says the Convener, "vapor of vapors! Everything is vapor."
verses.1:3: What advantage is there for man in all his toil at which he toils under the sun?
verses.1:4: One generation goes and another generation comes, yet the earth stands forever.
verses.1:5: The sun rises and the sun sets, and to its place it pants, rising there.
verses.1:6: Going toward the south and turning toward the north, turning and turning goes the wind, and upon its rounds the wind returns.
verses.1:7: All the streams go into the sea, yet the sea is not full; to the place where the streams go, there they return to go.
verses.1:8: All things are wearying; no one is able to speak of them. No eye is satisfied by seeing, and no ear is filled from hearing.
verses.1:9: What has been, that is what will be, and what has been done, that is what will be done; and there is not anything new under the sun.
verses.1:10: Is there a matter of which someone says, "Look, this is new"? It has already been in the ages that were before us.
verses.1:11: There is no remembrance of the former ones, and likewise for the later ones that will be, there will be no remembrance of them among those who will come afterward.
verses.1:12: I, the Convener, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.
verses.1:13: And I set my heart to inquire and to explore by wisdom concerning everything that is done under the heavens. It is a wretched task that God has given to the sons of man to be occupied with.
verses.1:14: I have seen all the deeds that are done under the sun, and look, everything is vapor and chasing wind.
verses.1:15: What is bent cannot become straight, and what is missing cannot be numbered.
verses.1:16: I spoke with my heart, saying, "Look, I have enlarged and increased wisdom beyond all who were before me over Jerusalem, and my heart has seen much wisdom and knowledge."
verses.1:17: And I set my heart to know wisdom and to know madness and folly; I came to know that this too is a striving for wind.
verses.1:18: For in an abundance of wisdom is an abundance of vexation, and one who adds knowledge adds pain.
verses.2:1: I said in my heart, "Come now, let me test you with gladness, and experience what is good." Yet look, that too was vapor.
verses.2:2: Of laughter I said, "Madness!" and of gladness, "What does this do?"
verses.2:3: I explored in my heart how to refresh my flesh with wine, while my heart guided me with wisdom, and how to grasp folly, until I might see what is good for the sons of man to do under the heavens for the number of the days of their life.
verses.2:4: I made my works great; I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
verses.2:5: I made gardens and orchards for myself, and I planted in them trees of every kind of fruit.
verses.2:6: I made pools of water for myself, to irrigate from them a forest sprouting trees.
verses.2:7: I bought male and female servants, and I had servants born in my house; I also had livestock of cattle and flocks in abundance, more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.
verses.2:8: I also collected for myself silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and of the provinces. I obtained for myself male and female singers, and the delights of the sons of man, concubine after concubine.
verses.2:9: Thus I grew great and increased beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem; moreover, my wisdom stood by me.
verses.2:10: And whatever my eyes asked for, I did not withhold from them; I did not keep my heart back from any gladness, for my heart was glad in all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.
verses.2:11: Then I turned toward all my works that my hands had done and toward the toil that I had toiled to do, and look, everything was vapor and chasing wind, and there was no advantage under the sun.
verses.2:12: And I turned to see wisdom, madness, and folly. For what can the man do who comes after the king? Only that which they have already done.
verses.2:13: And I saw that there is an advantage to wisdom over folly, like the advantage of light over darkness.
verses.2:14: The wise man has his eyes in his head, whereas the fool walks in darkness; yet I too came to know that one fate befalls all of them.
verses.2:15: Then I said in my heart, "Like the fate of the fool, it will happen to me as well; why then have I been exceedingly wise?" And I spoke in my heart that this too is vapor.
verses.2:16: For there is no remembrance forever of the wise man, just as of the fool, seeing that in the coming days everything will already have been forgotten; and how the wise man dies even as the fool!
verses.2:17: So I hated life, because the work that is done under the sun was distressing to me, for everything is vapor and chasing wind.
verses.2:18: And I hated all my toil at which I am toiling under the sun, because I must leave it behind to the man who will be after me.
verses.2:19: And who knows whether he will be wise or foolish? Yet he will rule over all my toil at which I toiled and acted wisely under the sun. This too is vapor.
verses.2:20: So I turned about to make my heart despair over all the toil at which I had toiled under the sun.
verses.2:21: For there is a man whose toil is with wisdom, knowledge, and skill, yet to a man who did not toil at it he must give it as his portion. This too is vapor and a great evil.
verses.2:22: For what comes to a man in all his toil and in the striving of his heart at which he toils under the sun?
verses.2:23: For all his days are pains, and his task is vexation; even in the night his heart does not lie still. This too is vapor.
verses.2:24: There is nothing better for a man than to eat and drink and let his soul see good in his toil. This too I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
verses.2:25: For who can eat and who can have enjoyment apart from me?
verses.2:26: For to a man who is good before Him, He has given wisdom, knowledge, and gladness; but to the sinner He has given the task of gathering and collecting, to give to the one who is good before God. This too is vapor and chasing wind.
verses.3:1: For everything there is an appointed season, and a time for every affair under the heavens:
verses.3:2: a time to give birth and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to pull up what has been planted;
verses.3:3: a time to kill and a time to heal; a time to break down and a time to build;
verses.3:4: a time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to lament and a time to dance;
verses.3:5: a time to cast stones and a time to collect stones; a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing;
verses.3:6: a time to search and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to cast aside;
verses.3:7: a time to tear and a time to sew; a time to remain silent and a time to speak;
verses.3:8: a time to love and a time to hate; a time of war and a time of peace.
verses.3:9: What advantage belongs to the worker in that at which he toils?
verses.3:10: I have seen the task that God has given to the sons of man to be occupied with.
verses.3:11: He has made everything fitting in its time; He has also placed eternity in their heart, yet so that man cannot discover the work that God has done from beginning even to end.
verses.3:12: I know that there is nothing better for them than to be glad and to do good during one's life.
verses.3:13: Moreover, that every man should eat and drink and see good in all his toil—that is a gift of God.
verses.3:14: I know that all that God does will endure forever; to it nothing can be added, and from it nothing can be subtracted. And God has done this so that people should fear before Him.
verses.3:15: What has been already is, and what is to be has already been; and God seeks out what is pursued.
verses.3:16: And further I saw under the sun: in the place of justice, there was wickedness; and in the place of righteousness, there was wickedness.
verses.3:17: I said in my heart, "God will judge the righteous and the wicked, for there is a time for every affair and for every deed there."
verses.3:18: I said in my heart concerning the sons of man, "It is for God to test them, and for them to see that they are beasts in themselves."
verses.3:19: For the fate of the sons of man and the fate of the beast—one fate belongs to them: as the death of the one, so is the death of the other, and all have one breath. And man has no advantage over the beast, for everything is vapor.
verses.3:20: All are going to one place; all came into being from the dust, and all are returning to the dust.
verses.3:21: Who knows whether the spirit of the sons of man ascends upward and whether the spirit of the beast descends downward to the earth?
verses.3:22: So I saw that there is nothing better than that a man should be glad in his works, for that is his portion. For who will bring him to see what will be after him?
verses.4:1: Then I turned again and saw all the oppressions that are carried out under the sun. Look, the tears of the oppressed, and there was no comforter for them; power lay in the hand of their oppressors, and there was no comforter for them.
verses.4:2: So I praised the dead, who have already died, above the living, who are still alive.
verses.4:3: Yet better than both of them is the one who has not yet come into being, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun.
verses.4:4: Then I saw all toil and all success in work, that it is a man's envy toward his neighbor. This too is futility and herding wind.
verses.4:5: The fool clasps his hands and devours his own flesh.
verses.4:6: Better is a palmful of rest than two handfuls of toil and herding wind.
verses.4:7: Then I turned again and saw futility under the sun.
verses.4:8: There is one alone without a second; indeed, he has neither son nor brother. Yet there is no end to all his toil, nor is his eye satisfied with wealth. "And for whom am I toiling and depriving my soul of good?" This too is futility, and it is a wretched business.
verses.4:9: Better are two than one, since there is a good reward for them in their toil.
verses.4:10: For if they fall, the one will raise up his partner; yet woe to the one who falls when there is no second to raise him up.
verses.4:11: Moreover, if two lie down, they become warm; but for one, how can he become warm?
verses.4:12: And if someone overpowers the one, the two will stand against him; and a three-ply cord is not swiftly snapped.
verses.4:13: Better is a poor and wise youth than an aged and foolish king who no longer knows how to be warned.
verses.4:14: For from prison he went out to reign, even though in his kingdom he was born poor.
verses.4:15: I saw all the living who walk about under the sun alongside the second youth who would stand in his place.
verses.4:16: There is no end to all the people, to all who existed before them; yet even those who come afterward will not rejoice in him. Surely this too is futility and striving for wind.
verses.4:17: Guard your foot when you go to the house of God; drawing near to listen is better than fools offering a sacrifice, for they do not realize that they are doing evil.
verses.5:1: Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring forth a word before God; for God is in heaven, and you are on the earth, so let your words be few.
verses.5:2: For a dream comes through an abundance of preoccupation, and a fool's voice through an abundance of words.
verses.5:3: When you vow a vow to God, do not delay in paying it, for there is no delight in fools. What you vow, pay.
verses.5:4: Better that you not vow than that you vow and not pay.
verses.5:5: Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before the messenger, "It was an error." Why should God grow angry at your voice and ruin the work of your hands?
verses.5:6: For in an abundance of dreams there are also futilities, and words in abundance; rather, fear God.
verses.5:7: If you see oppression of the poor and the plundering of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one high official watches above another high official, and high ones are over them.
verses.5:8: Yet the profit of a land in every respect is this: a king for a tilled field.
verses.5:9: One who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver, nor whoever loves abundance with revenue. This too is futility.
verses.5:10: When goods multiply, those who consume them multiply; and what benefit is there for their owner except looking on with his eyes?
verses.5:11: The worker's sleep is sweet, whether he eats little or much; yet the fullness of the rich man does not permit him to sleep.
verses.5:12: There is a sickening evil I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his own harm.
verses.5:13: And that wealth perishes in a bad business, and he fathers a son, yet there is nothing in his hand.
verses.5:14: Just as he came out of his mother's womb, naked he will depart again as he came, and he will take nothing from his toil that he may carry along in his hand.
verses.5:15: And this too is a sickening evil: in every way as he came, so he will go; and what profit is there for him that he toils for the wind?
verses.5:16: Moreover, all his days he eats in darkness, and he is greatly vexed, with his sickness and anger.
verses.5:17: Look, what I myself have seen is good and fitting: to eat and drink and see good in all his toil at which he toils under the sun during the numbered days of his life that God has given him, for that is his portion.
verses.5:18: Furthermore, as for every person to whom God has given wealth and possessions and granted power to eat from it and to receive his portion and to rejoice in his toil—this is a gift of God.
verses.5:19: For he will not often remember the days of his life, because God occupies him with the gladness of his heart.
verses.6:1: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy upon humanity:
verses.6:2: A man to whom God gives wealth, possessions, and honor, and he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he craves, yet God does not grant him power to eat from it; instead, a stranger eats it. This is futility, and it is an evil sickness.
verses.6:3: If a man fathers a hundred children and lives many years—however numerous the days of his years may be—yet his soul is not satisfied with good things, and he has no burial either, I say, "Better than he is a stillborn child."
verses.6:4: For in futility it comes, and in darkness it departs, and in darkness its name is shrouded.
verses.6:5: Moreover, it has neither seen nor known the sun; yet there is more rest for this one than for that one.
verses.6:6: And even if he lived a thousand years twice over, yet did not see good—is it not to one place that all are going?
verses.6:7: All a person's toil is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled.
verses.6:8: For what advantage is there for the wise person over the fool? What is there for the poor person who knows how to walk in the presence of the living?
verses.6:9: Better is what the eyes see than the roving of appetite. This too is futility and herding wind.
verses.6:10: What has been has already been called by name, and it is known what a human being is; and he cannot contend with one who is mightier than he.
verses.6:11: For there are many words that multiply futility; what advantage is there for a person?
verses.6:12: For who knows what is good for a person in life, throughout the numbered days of his life of futility, which he spends like a shadow? For who can declare to a person what will happen after him under the sun?
verses.7:1: A good name is better than choice oil, and the day of death than the day of one's birth.
verses.7:2: Going to a house of mourning is better than going to a house of feasting, because that is the end of every person, and the living will take it to heart.
verses.7:3: Grief is better than laughter, because through a sad face the heart grows better.
verses.7:4: The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning, while the heart of fools is in a house of gladness.
verses.7:5: Listening to the rebuke of a wise person is better than being someone who listens to the song of fools.
verses.7:6: For like the sound of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the fool; and this too is futility.
verses.7:7: For extortion makes a fool of a wise person, and a bribe ruins the heart.
verses.7:8: Better is the end of a matter than its beginning; better is one who is patient in spirit than one who is haughty in spirit.
verses.7:9: Do not be hasty in your spirit to become angry, because anger rests in the bosom of fools.
verses.7:10: Do not say, "How is it that the earlier days were better than these?" for you do not ask about this out of wisdom.
verses.7:11: Wisdom is good alongside an inheritance, and it is an advantage for those who see the sun.
verses.7:12: For to be in the shelter of wisdom is like being in the shelter of money, yet the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom keeps its possessors alive.
verses.7:13: Look at the work of God, for who can straighten what He has made crooked?
verses.7:14: On a day of prosperity be glad, and on a day of adversity reflect: God has made the one alongside the other, so that man cannot find out anything after him.
verses.7:15: I have seen all things in the days of my futility: there is a righteous person who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked person who prolongs his days in his evil.
verses.7:16: Do not be righteous to excess, and do not make yourself overly wise; why should you bring ruin on yourself?
verses.7:17: Do not act wickedly to excess, and do not be foolish; why die before your time?
verses.7:18: It is good that you take hold of this, and also do not let your hand drop from that, for the one who fears God will come through all of them.
verses.7:19: Wisdom gives greater strength to a wise person than ten rulers who are in a city.
verses.7:20: For there is no righteous person on earth who does good and does not sin.
verses.7:21: Also, do not take to heart all the words that people speak, so that you will not hear your servant cursing you.
verses.7:22: For many times your heart has known that you yourself have cursed others as well.
verses.7:23: All this I tested with wisdom; I said, "I will become wise," yet it was far from me.
verses.7:24: What has been is far away, and deep, so deep—who can find it?
verses.7:25: I turned, together with my heart, to know and to explore and to seek wisdom and a reckoning, and to know that wickedness is folly and that foolishness is madness.
verses.7:26: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is traps and nets, whose hands are fetters; one who is good before God will escape from her, but a sinner will be caught by her.
verses.7:27: "See, this is what I have found," said the Preacher, "putting one thing with another to find a reckoning,
verses.7:28: which my soul has still sought, yet I have not found: one man out of a thousand I have found, yet a woman among all these I have not found.
verses.7:29: Only look, this I have found: that God made mankind upright, yet they themselves have sought many schemes."
verses.8:1: Who is like the wise person, and who knows the interpretation of a matter? A person's wisdom brightens his face, and the sternness of his face is transformed.
verses.8:2: I say: Keep a king's command, and that because of the oath of God.
verses.8:3: Do not rush to go from his presence, and do not persist in an evil matter, for he does all that he desires.
verses.8:4: For a king's word has authority, and who can say to him, "What are you doing?"
verses.8:5: The one who keeps a command will know nothing evil, and a wise person's heart will know time and judgment.
verses.8:6: For every undertaking has a time and a judgment, though man's misery weighs heavily upon him.
verses.8:7: For he does not know what will happen; indeed, who will tell him how it will happen?
verses.8:8: No man has mastery over the spirit to hold back the spirit, and there is no authority over the day of death; there is no discharge in war, nor will wickedness rescue its possessors.
verses.8:9: All this I have seen, and I set my heart on every deed that is done under the sun—a time when man has ruled over man to his harm.
verses.8:10: And so I saw wicked people buried—those who used to enter and walk away from the holy place—and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is futility.
verses.8:11: Because a verdict against an evil deed is not carried out swiftly, the heart of the sons of man is filled within them to do evil.
verses.8:12: Even though a sinner does evil a hundred times and prolongs his days, yet I know that it will go well for those who fear God, who fear before Him.
verses.8:13: Yet it will not go well for the wicked person, and he will not prolong his days, like a shadow, because he does not fear before God.
verses.8:14: There is a futility that is done on the earth: there are righteous people to whom things come according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked people to whom things come according to the deeds of the righteous. I said that this too is futility.
verses.8:15: So I praised gladness, since there is nothing good for a person under the sun except to eat and to drink and to be glad, and this will accompany him in his toil during the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
verses.8:16: When I set my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth—even though neither by day nor by night does one see sleep with his eyes—
verses.8:17: then I saw all the work of God, that man is not able to find out the work that is done under the sun. No matter how much man toils to seek it, he will not find it; and even if the wise person claims to know, he is not able to find it.
verses.9:1: For all this I took to my heart, examining all of it: that the righteous and the wise and their deeds are in the hand of God. Whether it is love or hatred, man does not know; everything lies before them.
verses.9:2: Everything is the same for all: there is one fate for the righteous and for the wicked, for the good, and for the clean and the unclean, for the one who sacrifices and for the one who does not sacrifice. As the good person is, so is the sinner; the one who swears an oath is like the one who fears an oath.
verses.9:3: This is an evil in everything that is done under the sun: that one fate belongs to all. Moreover, the heart of the sons of man is full of evil, and madness is in their hearts while they live, and afterward—to the dead.
verses.9:4: For anyone who is joined to all the living has confidence, because a living dog is better than a dead lion.
verses.9:5: For the living know that they will die, yet the dead know nothing at all; they no longer have any reward, because their memory has been forgotten.
verses.9:6: Their love, along with their hatred and their envy, has already perished, and they no longer have any portion forever in all that is done under the sun.
verses.9:7: Go, eat your bread in gladness, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, because God has already accepted your works.
verses.9:8: At all times let your clothes be white, and never let oil be missing from your head.
verses.9:9: Enjoy life with the wife you love throughout all the days of your futile life that He has given you under the sun—all your futile days—for that is your portion in life and in your toil as you toil under the sun.
verses.9:10: Everything your hand finds to do, do with your strength, because there is no work or reckoning or knowledge or wisdom in Sheol, where you are going.
verses.9:11: Once more I saw under the sun that the race does not belong to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty, nor bread to the wise, nor wealth to those of understanding, nor favor to the knowledgeable, for time and chance happen to all of them.
verses.9:12: Indeed, man does not even know his time: like fish caught in a cruel net and like birds caught in a snare, like them the sons of man are ensnared at an evil time, when it suddenly falls on them.
verses.9:13: This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it appeared great to me:
verses.9:14: There was a small city, and the men in it were few; and a great king came against it, surrounded it, and built great siegeworks against it.
verses.9:15: And a poor wise man was found in it, and he rescued the city by his wisdom; still, no one remembered that poor man.
verses.9:16: So I said, "Wisdom is better than might, yet the wisdom of the poor man is scorned, and his words are not heard."
verses.9:17: Words of the wise are better heard in quietness than the outcry of a ruler among fools.
verses.9:18: Wisdom is better than weapons of battle, yet a single sinner ruins much good.
verses.10:1: Dead flies cause a perfumer's oil to stink and ferment; a little folly is heavier than wisdom and honor.
verses.10:2: The heart of a wise man is toward his right, and the heart of a fool is toward his left.
verses.10:3: And even along the road, when a fool walks, his heart is lacking, and he says to all that he is a fool.
verses.10:4: If the spirit of the ruler rises against you, do not give up your post, for calmness puts great offenses to rest.
verses.10:5: There is an evil I saw under the sun, like an error going out from before the ruler:
verses.10:6: Folly is placed in many lofty positions, while the wealthy sit in a low place.
verses.10:7: I saw slaves on horses, and officials walking like slaves on the ground.
verses.10:8: One who digs a pit will fall into it, and a snake will bite one who breaches a wall.
verses.10:9: One who quarries stones will be injured by them; one who splits logs will be put in danger by them.
verses.10:10: If the iron becomes dull and he has not sharpened the edge, then he must exert greater strength, yet wisdom has the advantage of bringing success.
verses.10:11: If the snake bites without a charm, then there is no advantage for the master of the tongue.
verses.10:12: The words of a wise man's mouth are grace, while the lips of a fool swallow him up.
verses.10:13: The start of the words of his mouth is folly, and the end of his speech is wicked madness.
verses.10:14: And the fool multiplies words. Man does not know what will be, and what will be after him, who can tell him?
verses.10:15: The toil of fools wearies him, because he does not know how to go to a city.
verses.10:16: Woe to you, land, whose king is a youth and whose officials eat in the morning!
verses.10:17: Happy are you, land, whose king is a son of nobles and whose officials eat at the right time, for strength and not for drunkenness!
verses.10:18: Through sheer laziness the roof beams sag, and through slackness of hands the house leaks.
verses.10:19: For laughter they prepare a meal, and wine makes life glad, and money answers it all.
verses.10:20: Even in your mind, do not curse a king, and in your bedchambers, do not curse a wealthy man; for a bird of the sky will carry the voice, and a winged creature will report the matter.
verses.11:1: Send out your bread across the surface of the waters, for you will find it when many days have passed.
verses.11:2: Give a share to seven, and even to eight, because you do not know what calamity will happen on the earth.
verses.11:3: If the clouds are filled with rain, they empty onto the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will be.
verses.11:4: One who observes the wind will not sow, and one who gazes at the clouds will not harvest.
verses.11:5: Just as you do not know what the way of the wind is, nor how bones form in the womb of a pregnant woman, in the same way you do not know the work of God, who makes all things.
verses.11:6: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not let your hand rest, because you do not know which one will succeed, this or that, or whether both of them will be equally good.
verses.11:7: And sweet is the light, and seeing the sun is good for the eyes.
verses.11:8: For if a man lives many years, he should rejoice in all of them, yet remember the days of darkness, because they will be many. All that is coming is vapor.
verses.11:9: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart make you glad in the days of your young manhood; walk in the paths of your heart and in the sights of your eyes, yet know that concerning all these things God will bring you to judgment.
verses.11:10: And remove vexation from your heart, and put trouble away from your flesh, because youth and dark hair are vapor.
verses.12:1: And remember your Creator in the days of your young manhood, before the days of adversity come and years arrive about which you will say, "I take no delight in them";
verses.12:2: before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars turn dark, and the clouds come back after the rain;
verses.12:3: on the day when the guards of the house tremble, and the men of strength become stooped, and the grinding women fall idle because they have grown few, and those peering through the windows grow dark,
verses.12:4: and the double doors onto the street are closed when the sound of the mill drops low, and one rises at the sound of the bird, and all the daughters of song sink down.
verses.12:5: Moreover, they fear heights, and terrors are along the road; the almond tree blooms, the grasshopper drags itself heavily, and the caperberry fails, because man is going to his everlasting home, and the mourners walk around in the street.
verses.12:6: Before the cord of silver is snapped, and the bowl of gold is crushed, and a jar is broken at the spring, and the wheel is crushed into the cistern,
verses.12:7: and the dust goes back to the earth just as it was, and the spirit goes back to God, who gave it.
verses.12:8: "Vapor of vapors," said the Assembler, "everything is vapor."
verses.12:9: And beyond being wise, the Assembler also taught knowledge to the people; he weighed, investigated, and set in order many proverbs.
verses.12:10: The Assembler sought to find words of delight, and written in uprightness were words of truth.
verses.12:11: Words of wise men are like goads, and like driven nails are the masters of collections; they were given from one Shepherd.
verses.12:12: And beyond these, my son, be warned: there is no end to making many books, and much study brings weariness to the flesh.
verses.12:13: The conclusion of the matter; everything has been heard. Fear God and observe His commandments, because this is the whole of man.
verses.12:14: For God will bring every deed to judgment, together with everything concealed, whether good or evil.

notes.1:1: Hebrew Qoheleth is a feminine singular Qal participle of qahal ("to assemble, convene"), used as an official title for one who convenes or addresses an assembly (traditionally rendered "the Preacher" or "the Teacher").
notes.1:2: Hebrew hevel literally means "vapor" or "breath," used throughout the book for what is fleeting, ungraspable, and empty (often rendered "vanity" or "futility"); "vapor of vapors" is a Hebrew superlative construction.
notes.1:13: Hebrew la'anot bo (Qal infinitive construct of 'anah, "to be occupied with," cognate with 'inyan, "task") may also play on the homonymous root 'anah ("to be afflicted, humbled"), conveying a burdensome occupation.
notes.1:14: Hebrew re'ut ruach derives either from a late Hebrew/Aramaic root meaning "striving, pursuit" ("chasing wind") or from ra'ah ("to shepherd, herd," as in Hosea 12:1, MT 12:2), depicting a futile attempt to capture the wind.
notes.1:17: Hebrew sikluth ("folly") is here spelled with sin rather than samekh (contrast 2:3, 12, 13), an orthographic variant that also creates a subtle visual echo of sekel ("insight, prudence").
notes.2:3: Hebrew limshokh (Qal infinitive construct of mashakh, literally "to draw, pull, sustain") with "wine" and "my flesh" idiomatically expresses refreshing, stimulating, or cheering the body with wine.
notes.2:8: Hebrew shiddah weshiddot ("a shiddah and shiddot," denoting multiplicity) occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; its exact sense is uncertain, most commonly understood in context as "many concubines" (though rabbinic Hebrew uses shiddah for a chest or litter).
notes.2:24: The Masoretic text lacks an explicit comparative particle ("than"), reading literally "there is nothing good for a man that he should eat and drink..."; it is usually understood elliptically as "nothing better... than" (compare 3:12, 22), though some read it as "it is not in a man's own power to eat and drink."
notes.2:25: The Masoretic text reads mimmenni ("apart from me"), whereas the Septuagint and Syriac reflect mimmennu ("apart from Him"); the rare verb yachush probably means "have enjoyment" or "feel" (from a late Hebrew/Aramaic root), though the homonymous verb chush means "hasten."
notes.3:2: Hebrew laledet is the Qal active infinitive construct of yalad, literally "to give birth," though often rendered passively as "to be born" (contrast the Niphal form for being born in 7:1).
notes.3:11: Hebrew yafeh means "beautiful" or "fitting"; ha'olam ("eternity" or "perpetuity") denotes a sense of timeless duration beyond human grasp (some also connect it with later senses of "the world" or "obscurity").
notes.3:15: Hebrew nirdaf is a Niphal participle of radaf ("to pursue"), literally "what is pursued" or "what is driven away"; it is variously understood of past events that God brings back again or of the persecuted person whom God seeks out to vindicate (linking to 3:16-17).
notes.3:17: The Masoretic text ends with sham ("there," echoing shammah in 3:16 and referring to the sphere of God's judgment); some scholars repoint the consonants as sam ("He has appointed").
notes.3:21: The Masoretic vocalization of ha'olah and hayyoredet matches the definite article ("that ascends... that descends"), though the following pronoun hi ("it") and comparable Masoretic interrogative vocalizations (e.g., Lev 10:19; Num 16:22) support the interrogative sense "whether it ascends... whether it descends."
notes.4:1: The Hebrew repeats the exact form ha'ashuqim in two senses—first as the abstract plural "oppressions" and second as the Qal passive participle "the oppressed"—alongside the Qal active participle "their oppressors" from the same root ('ashaq).
notes.4:4: Hebrew hevel ("futility") literally means "vapor" or "breath," denoting what is fleeting and insubstantial. The phrase re'ut ruach ("herding wind") derives from Hebrew ra'ah ("to shepherd, herd"), though an Aramaic cognate sense of "longing or vexation of spirit" is also possible.
notes.4:8: The Qere reads singular 'eno ("his eye," matching the feminine singular verb tisba'), whereas the Ketiv has plural 'enav ("his eyes"). The Hebrew shifts abruptly without an introductory verb into the first-person question, "And for whom am I toiling...?"
notes.4:16: The clause "to all who existed before them" (literally "to all that was before them") mirrors Ecclesiastes' idiom in 1:16 and 2:9, though some take the suffix on lifnehem as resumptive, yielding "all those before whom he stood," that is, all whom he led.
notes.4:17: The Qere reads singular raglekha ("your foot"), whereas the Ketiv reads the plural form ("your feet"). The Qal infinitive absolute qarov ("drawing near") forms an elliptical comparison before the preposition min ("than"), and la'asot ra' (literally "to do evil") serves as the complement of the participle "knowing."
notes.5:6: The Masoretic Hebrew is notably terse ("For in an abundance of dreams and futilities and words in abundance"), with the conjunction on "futilities" introducing the predicate; the second ki is adversative ("rather").
notes.5:8: The Qere reads masculine hu' (agreeing with masculine yitron, "profit"), while the Ketiv reads feminine hi' (agreeing with feminine 'erets, "land"). The concise closing phrase melekh lesadeh ne'evad is difficult: the Niphal participle ne'evad may modify "field" ("a king for a tilled field") or "king" ("a king is served by a field").
notes.5:10: The Qere reads re'ut ("looking, seeing"), a late Hebrew feminine noun form, while the Ketiv spells the rarer synonymous form re'it.
notes.5:16: The Masoretic text vocalizes vekha'as as a Qal perfect verb ("and he is vexed") modified by the adverb "greatly," followed by the abrupt nominal phrase "and his sickness and anger."
notes.5:19: The Hiphil participle ma'aneh derives from 'anah III ("to be occupied," cognate with Ecclesiastes' recurring noun 'inyan, "business/occupation"), hence "occupies him"; some derive it from 'anah I ("to answer"), yielding "answers him with the gladness of his heart."
notes.6:7: Hebrew nefesh ("soul, life") carries its concrete sense of "appetite" or "craving" here (paired with "his mouth") and in 6:9 ("roving of appetite"), and the Niphal verb timmale' literally means "be filled."
notes.6:10: The Qere reads shettaqqif ("one who is mightier") without the definite article, whereas the Ketiv includes the article ("the one who is mightier"). The preceding clause ("it is known what a human being is") may also be rendered "it is known that he is human."
notes.6:12: The Qal verb ya'asem (literally "he makes them," with plural suffix referring to "days") is an idiom for spending or passing time, here compared to a fleeting shadow.
notes.7:12: The Hebrew wording is compressed, literally "for in the shadow/shelter of wisdom, in the shadow/shelter of silver," using repeated prepositions to draw a parallel between the protection offered by wisdom and money.
notes.7:18: The idiom "will come through all of them" literally reads "will go out with/from all of them" (Qal imperfect of yatsa with the direct object marker), meaning either to emerge safely from both extremes or to fulfill both obligations.
notes.7:22: The Ketiv (written text) has the defective form of the second-person pronoun while the Qere (read text) supplies the standard masculine singular form "you"; both convey the same meaning.
notes.7:27: The Masoretic Hebrew reads the feminine singular perfect verb "said" to agree with the grammatical feminine form of the title Qohelet (literally "Assembler" or "Speaker," traditionally rendered "the Preacher").
notes.8:2: The opening independent pronoun "I" stands elliptically without an explicit verb of speaking ("I [say]"), and "command" is literally "mouth" of a king.
notes.8:8: The Hebrew noun ruach can mean either "spirit" (the life-breath departing at death, matching "the day of death") or "wind" (impossible to confine).
notes.8:10: This verse has famously compressed Hebrew syntax; the Masoretic verb is a Hithpael imperfect of shakach ("were forgotten"), whereas some ancient versions reflect a similar root meaning "were praised."
notes.8:17: The rare Late Biblical Hebrew compound conjunction beshel asher (literally "in that which") functions concessively here to mean "no matter how much" or "however hard."
notes.9:2: The Masoretic Text lists only three terms in the middle series ("for the good, and for the clean and the unclean") without adding "and for the evil/bad," which some ancient versions supply for symmetry.
notes.9:4: The Qere (read text) has the Pual imperfect of chavar ("is joined"), translated here, while the Ketiv (written text) reads the root bachar ("chooses" or "is chosen").
notes.9:9: The Masoretic Text repeats the phrase "all your futile days" for emphasis, whereas some ancient versions omit the repetition.
notes.9:15: The opening verb is an impersonal Qal active third-person singular ("one found," idiomatically "was found"), and the Piel perfect "he rescued" can also be taken modally as "he could have rescued."
notes.10:1: Hebrew joins two Hiphil imperfect verbs without a conjunction (yav'ish yabbia', 'cause to stink, cause to bubble/ferment') and uses yaqar ('heavy/weighty') to describe a little folly outweighing wisdom and honor.
notes.10:3: The written ketiv reads 'when the fool' (with the definite article), while the read qere followed here reads 'when a fool' (indefinite). The final clause can alternatively mean he says concerning everyone else that he is a fool.
notes.10:10: Hebrew panim ('face') refers to the blade's cutting edge, paired with the Pilpel verb qilqal ('sharpen'). The terse closing clause uses the Hiphil infinitive of kshr ('bringing success') to state wisdom's advantage.
notes.10:15: The Hebrew shifts from plural 'fools' (ha-kesilim) to distributive singular 'him' and 'he,' and pairs the normally masculine noun 'toil' (amal) with a feminine Piel verb (teyagge'ennu).
notes.10:20: The written ketiv reads 'the wings' (with the definite article), while the read qere followed here omits the article ('wings'; literally 'a master of wings').
notes.11:3: Hebrew yehu' is a rare Aramaizing Qal imperfect form of the verb hwh ('to be'), written with a final silent aleph.
notes.11:5: Hebrew ha-ruach can mean either 'the wind' (as in 11:4) or 'the spirit/breath,' and the elliptical phrase ka'atsamim literally reads 'like the bones,' understood either as a second parallel mystery or as how the spirit enters the bones.
notes.11:10: Hebrew shacharut occurs only here and is derived either from shachor ('blackness,' referring to the dark hair of youth) or from shachar ('dawn,' i.e., the dawn of life).
notes.12:5: Hebrew yane'ts is a Hiphil imperfect meaning 'blossoms' (spelled with an orthographic aleph), and ha-'aviyyonah (occurring only here) denotes the caperberry, an ancient stimulant often rendered 'desire' by connection with the root meaning 'to desire.'
notes.12:6: The written ketiv reads yirchaq ('is removed' or 'grows distant'), while the read qere followed here reads yerateq (Niphal imperfect, 'is snapped' or 'severed').
notes.12:8: Hebrew hevel literally means 'vapor' or 'breath,' used metaphorically for transience or futility; ha-Qoheleth ('the Assembler') is a title derived from the root qhl ('to assemble').
notes.12:10: The Masoretic Text vocalizes katuv as a Qal passive participle ('written'), rather than an active finite verb ('wrote').
notes.12:11: Hebrew ba'ale asuppot literally means 'masters of collections,' referring either to compilers/sages of wisdom assemblies or idiomatically to 'collected sayings.'
